# Use Ubuntu 22.04 base image with bash
FROM --platform=linux/x86_64 ubuntu:22.04

ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# Install system dependencies: git, curl, wget, build tools, python3.10, python3-pip, and other essentials
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    curl \
    wget \
    build-essential \
    python3.10 \
    python3.10-venv \
    python3.10-distutils \
    python3-pip \
    python3-setuptools \
    python3-wheel \
    libffi-dev \
    locales \
    locales-all \
    tzdata \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set python3 to point to python3.10 explicitly and pip to python3-pip
RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.10 1 \
    && update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python python /usr/bin/python3.10 1 \
    && python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip

# Create workdir
WORKDIR /testbed/

# Clone the target repository and checkout the specific commit SHA, then install dependencies with poetry
# Poetry installation from official recommended script
RUN curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | POETRY_HOME=/opt/poetry python3.10 - && \
    ln -s /opt/poetry/bin/poetry /usr/local/bin/poetry

# Clone repo and checkout specified commit. Install dependencies using poetry in virtual env mode
ARG COMMIT_SHA=04c71d7d297447479d897b6803206210ed589d53
RUN git clone https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer.git /testbed && \
    cd /testbed && \
    git reset --hard $COMMIT_SHA && \
    # Configure poetry to create virtual env inside the project
    poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true && \
    poetry install --no-interaction --no-ansi

# Set bashrc to activate the poetry environment automatically on starting a shell inside container
RUN echo "source /testbed/.venv/bin/activate" >> /root/.bashrc

# Export environment variable note for OPENAI_API_KEY (will be set externally for tests)
ENV OPENAI_API_KEY=""

# Default shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as base image for broad compatibility and bash shell availability
FROM --platform=linux/x86_64 ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid interactive tzdata dialogs during build
ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# Install essential system packages and tools, correcting python package names for Ubuntu 22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    wget \
    git \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    ca-certificates \
    locales \
    locales-all \
    tzdata \
    python3 \
    python3-venv \
    python3-pip \
    python3-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Upgrade pip to latest in the python3 context
RUN python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip

# Create and activate a Python virtual environment called 'testbed'
RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venvs/testbed
ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venvs/testbed
ENV PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"

# Ensure pip, setuptools and wheel are installed in the venv
RUN pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /testbed/

# Clone target repository and checkout the specified commit
RUN git clone https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope.git /testbed && \
    git reset --hard f761cf215fbd1f0a1e57eb2d073229628b77f462

# Install the project in editable mode with all extras including distribute, full and dev
RUN pip install -e . && \
    pip install -e ".[distribute]" && \
    pip install -e ".[full]" && \
    pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Install pre-commit hooks (as per context retrieval agent instructions)
RUN pre-commit install || echo "pre-commit not installed or failed, ignored"

# Add bashrc to activate venv by default in interactive sessions
RUN echo "source $VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/activate" >> /root/.bashrc

Some questions about reset_equipped_tools
I noticed that this tool requires the model to pass in a group name and a boolean value to activate a tool group, but I didn't find any operation to close the tool group. So if the tool is called a second time, will the tool group that was activated the first time remain active?

You've identified a bug in the meta tool function—we failed to deactivate the tools properly. We'll fix this as soon as possible. Thanks for pointing it out!

The error you're encountering, `Object of type Image is not JSON serializable`, indicates that the image file is not being properly serialized before being stored in the database. To resolve this, you need to ensure that the image is converted to a JSON-serializable format, such as a base64-encoded string.

Langflow provides utility methods for handling this conversion. Here’s how you can address the issue:

1. **Convert the Image to Base64**: Use the `pil_to_base64` function to convert the image to a base64-encoded string.

   ```python
   from PIL import Image as PILImage
   from io import BytesIO
   import base64

   def pil_to_base64(image: PILImage) -> str:
       buffered = BytesIO()
       image.save(buffered, format="PNG")
       img_str = base64.b64encode(buffered.getvalue())
       return img_str.decode("utf-8")
   ```

2. **Update the `ChatInput` Node**: Modify the `ChatInput` node to convert the image file to a base64 string before storing it.

   ```python
   class ChatInput(ChatComponent):
       # ... other code ...

       def message_response(self) -> Message:
           # Convert image files to base64
           base64_files = []
           for file in self.files:
               if isinstance(file, Image):
                   base64_files.append(pil_to_base64(file))
               else:
                   base64_files.append(file)

           message = Message(
               text=self.input_value,
               sender=self.sender,
               sender_name=self.sender_name,
               session_id=self.session_id,
               files=base64_files,
           )

           if (
               self.session_id
               and isinstance(message, Message)
               and isinstance(message.text, str)
               and self.should_store_message
           ):
               store_message(
                   message,
                   flow_id=self.graph.flow_id,
               )
               self.message.value = message

           self.status = message
           return message
   ```

3. **Ensure Proper Serialization**: Make sure the `Message` class and any related serialization logic handle the base64-encoded string correctly.

By converting the image to a base64 string, you ensure that it is JSON-serializable and can be stored in the database without issues.
